instruction: I find Georgia more elegant for reading long articles online. Could you change Chrome's serif font to Georgia?

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the serif font family to Georgia. The evaluator checks if the serif_font_family in Chrome preferences matches 'Georgia' (case-insensitive). Serif fonts are used when websites specifically request serif-style fonts in their CSS.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts Chrome serif font from webkit.webprefs.fonts.serif.Zyyy path in Preferences file
Metric implements appropriate case-insensitive comparison for font name matching
Postconfig properly restarts Chrome to ensure preferences are flushed to disk before verification
Complete coverage: instruction has one requirement (change serif font to Georgia) and evaluator verifies exactly that
Expected value 'Georgia' is semantically correct and matches the instruction requirement
Logic flow is sound: user action -> Chrome saves -> postconfig restarts -> getter reads -> metric compares
Edge cases handled: file reading errors have try/catch with fallback, multi-OS support implemented
State accessibility confirmed: getter can access saved preferences after Chrome restart
